exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 25–38, $$A$$ denotes an $$m \times n$$ matrix. Mark each statement True or False (T/F). Justify each answer.

problem.paragraph: (T/F) The null space of $$A$$ is the solution set of the equation $$A\textbf{x} = 0$$ .
(T/F) A null space is a vector space.
(T/F) The null space of an $$m \times n$$ matrix is in $$\mathbb{R}^{m}$$ .
(T/F) The column space of an $$m \times n$$ matrix is in $$\mathbb{R}^{m}$$ .
(T/F) The column space of $$A$$ is the range of the mapping $$\left. \textbf{x}\mapsto A\textbf{x} \right.$$ .
(T/F) $$\text{Col} A$$ is the set of all solutions of $$A\textbf{x} = \textbf{b}$$ .
(T/F) If the equation $$A\textbf{x} = \textbf{b}$$ is consistent, then $$\text{Col} A = \mathbb{R}^{m}$$ .
(T/F) Nul $$A$$ is the kernel of the mapping $$\left. \textbf{x}\mapsto A\textbf{x} \right.$$ .
(T/F) The kernel of a linear transformation is a vector space.
(T/F) The range of a linear transformation is a vector space.
(T/F) Col $$A$$ is the set of all vectors that can be written as $$A\textbf{x}$$ for some $$\textbf{x}$$ .
(T/F) The set of all solutions of a homogeneous linear differential equation is the kernel of a linear transformation.
(T/F) The row space of $$A$$ is the same as the column space of $$A^{T}$$ .
(T/F) The null space of $$A$$ is the same as the row space of $$A^{T}$$ .

problem.paragraph: First method: $$W$$ is a subspace of $$\mathbb{R}^{3}$$ by Theorem 2 because $$W$$ is the set of all solutions to a system of homogeneous linear equations (where the system has only one equation). Equivalently, $$W$$ is the null space of the $$1 \times 3$$ matrix $$A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & {- 3} & {- 1} \end{bmatrix}$$ .

Second method: Solve the equation $$a - 3b - c = 0$$ for the leading variable $$a$$ in terms of the free variables $$b$$ and $$c$$ . Any solution has the form $$\begin{bmatrix} {3b + c} \\ b \\ c \end{bmatrix},$$ where $$b$$ and $$c$$ are arbitrary, and $$\left[\right. \begin{matrix}3 b + c \\ b \\ c\end{matrix} \left]\right. & = & b \left[\right. \begin{matrix}3 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{matrix} \left]\right. & + & c \left[\right. \begin{matrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{matrix} \left]\right. & & \uparrow & & \uparrow & & \mathbf{v}_{1} & & \mathbf{v}_{2}$$

This calculation shows that $$W = \text{Span} \left\{ \mathbf{v}_{1} \text{,} \mathbf{v}_{2} \right\}$$ . Thus $$W$$ is a subspace of $$\mathbb{R}^{3}$$ by Theorem 1. We could also solve the equation $$a - 3b - c = 0$$ for $$b$$ or $$c$$ and get alternative descriptions of $$W$$ as a set of linear combinations of two vectors.

Both $$\textbf{v}$$ and $$\mathbf{w}$$ are in Col $$A$$ . Since Col $$A$$ is a vector space, $$\textbf{v} + \textbf{w}$$ must be in Col $$A$$ . That is, the equation $$A\textbf{x} = \textbf{v} + \textbf{w}$$ is consistent.

Let $$\textbf{x}$$ be any vector in $${\mathbb{R}}^{n}$$ . Notice $$A\textbf{x}$$ is in Col $$A$$ , since it is a linear combination of the columns of $$A$$ . Since $$\text{Col} A = \text{Nul} A$$ , the vector $$A\textbf{x}$$ is also in Nul $$A$$ . Hence $$A^{2}\textbf{x} = A(A\textbf{x}) = 0$$ establishing that every vector $$\textbf{x}$$ from $$\mathbb{R}^{n}$$ is in Nul $$A^{2}$$ .
